claims.text: Since Chrome 148 on 5 May 2026, any web page can talk to Gemini Nano through the Prompt API on the reader's own machine, with no network once the model is downloaded.
claims.quote: Since Chrome 148, released on 5 May 2026, any web page can talk to a language model that runs on the reader's own machine.

claims.text: For the client-side pattern this is the most important piece so far and the hardest, because intelligence was the piece that kept a back end in the picture.
claims.quote: Intelligence was the piece that kept a back end in the picture.

claims.text: As of today the newsroom's payments are live, on a Stripe link and nothing of the newsroom's own.
claims.quote: the newsroom's payments are live, on a Stripe link and nothing of ours

claims.text: The Summarizer, Translator and Language Detector APIs have been stable since Chrome 138; Writer, Rewriter and Proofreader are still developer trials.
claims.quote: The Summarizer, Translator and Language Detector APIs have been stable since 138.

claims.text: The Prompt API accepts text, images and audio, returns text optionally constrained by a JSON schema, keeps and clones sessions, and supports five languages: English, Japanese, Spanish, German and French.
claims.quote: Five languages so far: English, Japanese, Spanish, German and French.

claims.text: Native tool use in the Prompt API is experimental and behind a flag; what works is structured output, and WebMCP, which lets a site describe its tools to the reader's agent, is a separate API in origin trial.
claims.quote: Native tool use in the Prompt API is experimental and behind a flag.

claims.text: Gemini Nano is a model in the 2 to 4 billion parameter range that Chrome downloads once per device, not once per site.
claims.quote: a model in the 2 to 4 billion parameter range that Chrome downloads once per device, not once per site

claims.text: The model needs a desktop with at least 22 GB free on the disk with the Chrome profile, and either a GPU with more than 4 GB of video memory or 16 GB of RAM and four cores.
claims.quote: At least 22 GB free on the disk with the Chrome profile.

claims.text: The owner's first download had a banner with no sense of time, vanished on refresh, and the model turned up by the morning, with network traffic the only sign of life.
claims.quote: I left the laptop open overnight, and by the morning the model was there.

claims.text: The download did not stop: it continues in the background after a refresh or close and resumes after a restart; the progress bar is the page's job, and the demo pages did not ask again.
claims.quote: The progress bar is the page's job.

claims.text: The model is roughly 4 GB, downloaded once per device and shared by every site; Chrome deletes it if free disk space falls below about 10 GB.
claims.quote: It is roughly 4 GB, downloaded once per device.

claims.text: The first thing worth shipping is a small honest component that shows bytes, rate and time remaining, survives a refresh, says it is safe to close the tab, and lists likely reasons when a device is unavailable.
claims.quote: That is the first thing worth shipping.

claims.text: There are surprisingly few good examples of the Prompt API in action: Chrome's case studies are real but narrow and mostly use the task APIs.
claims.quote: I looked for good examples of the Prompt API in action, and found surprisingly few.

claims.text: The reasons are real: five months on the open web, a gated desktop audience, a 4 GB first run, a small model, five languages, tool calling not ready, and the standards fight.
claims.quote: Teams that try it as a chatbot are disappointed; teams that try it as a function are not.

claims.text: Chrome shipped the Prompt API over formal opposition from Mozilla, Apple's WebKit team, the W3C Technical Architecture Group and Microsoft.
claims.quote: Chrome shipped the Prompt API over formal opposition.

claims.text: Mozilla's position is that the API has severe negative consequences to the interoperability, updatability and neutrality of the web platform.
claims.quote: severe negative consequences to the interoperability, updatability, and neutrality of the web platform

claims.text: The objections come down to three things: prompts do not travel between browsers' models, a vendor's usage policy sits in front of a web API, and the browser decides which model and version.
claims.quote: A vendor policy sits in front of a web API.

claims.text: The owner agrees with most of the objections, since a model he cannot pin, version or inspect is not sovereign infrastructure, but does not think the answer is to wait.
claims.quote: But I do not think the answer is to wait.

claims.text: Edge already offers the same API shape on its own models, Phi-4-mini and Aion, so the interface is not Chrome's alone even if the standards process is unfinished.
claims.quote: so the interface is not Chrome's alone, even if the standards process is unfinished

claims.text: The discipline that limits the damage: keep the meaning in the data not the prompt, use the model as a function not an oracle, and always have a path without it.
claims.quote: Keep the meaning in the data, not in the prompt.

claims.text: The five readers' graph answered a question about any of 45 concepts in a median of 2,579 tokens, every statement anchored, against 25,698 tokens to read the five articles.
claims.quote: a median of 2,579 tokens, with every statement anchored to its sentence, against 25,698 tokens to read the five articles

value.unit: median tokens for a graph answer against reading the five articles

claims.text: A context window measured in thousands of tokens cannot hold the five articles but can hold the graph's answer, and the anchors mean every answer can show its sources.
claims.quote: It can hold the graph's answer, with room left for the question.

claims.text: A local model can infer personas from the text a reader reads without anything leaving the browser, and transcribe and structure a voice memo on the device before it is encrypted into a vault lane.
claims.quote: a memo could be transcribed and structured on the device before it is encrypted into a vault lane

claims.text: The synthetic readers found 51 missing figures out of 527; a local model can describe what each figure shows and say when it differs from its caption.
claims.quote: found 51 missing figures out of 527

claims.text: The first four opportunities share one property: the model never decides anything important on its own; it answers from anchors, labels into a fixed set or transcribes, and the page or the person checks.
claims.quote: the model never decides anything important on its own

claims.text: A behaviour-policy helper for RiskMandate could classify each rule a user writes as boundary, setting, expectation or none, privately, as a draft for a person to check.
claims.quote: Classifies each rule a user writes as boundary, setting, expectation or none, privately

claims.text: A local second reader that checks a draft against rules and sources is only partly ready: the model is too small to be the only check.
claims.quote: Partly: too small to be the only check

claims.text: A vault is being built alongside the article with a test page per capability, measured on real machines, with the numbers published.
claims.quote: A vault is being built alongside this article to explore all of this properly

claims.text: The model status panel is an open component in the spirit of SG Meter: it checks eligibility, shows progress with bytes, rate and time, survives a refresh, and explains in plain words why a device cannot run the model.
claims.quote: An open component, in the spirit of SG Meter

claims.text: No measurements of speed or quality are claimed here; those are what the vault is for.
claims.quote: No measurements of speed or quality are claimed here; those are what the vault is for.

claims.text: The measurements to publish: download time, time to first token, tokens per second, context window, and accuracy against the anchors, on the machines the newsroom has.
claims.quote: These are the numbers missing from almost every piece about Gemini Nano, including this one.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo after the owner first tried Gemini Nano; an agent in a separate Claude session researched and drafted it, and where impressions and documentation disagreed the article follows the documentation.
claims.quote: the article follows the documentation and says so

claims.text: The site's agent gave the draft a last pass with plainer wording and a correction to the claim that renting was the only way to put a model behind a page.
claims.quote: a correction to the claim that renting was the only way to put a model behind a page
